Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:10:1.english: During the first three hours - At the time of [divine] wrath.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:11:1.english: [The prayer] of the morning as well - In the morning prayer [the Yotzer prayer].

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:11:2.hebrew: צבורא מצלו - שחרית בכל מקומות. תפלת מוספין, הואיל וזמנה כל היום, והיא שיחת שחרית וצהרים, יש שמתפללין אותה בבקר, ויש מאחרין:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:11:2.english: A community is praying - Shacharit [is prayed] in all places. [As for] the Musaf prayer, since its time is all day, and it is a prayer of morning and midday, some pray it in the morning, and some delay [it].

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:12:1.hebrew: והא אמרת - ראשונות יושב ועוסק בתורה, שניות דן, והכא אמרת בקמייתא דן:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:12:1.english: But didn't you say - [During the] first [three hours] He sits and engages in Torah, [and during the] second [three hours] He judges; and here you say [that] in the first [three hours] He judges.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:13:1.english: Buy the truth - Incur expenses for the study of Torah.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:13:2.english: And do not sell [it] - Teach others for free.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:13:3.hebrew:
דין לא כתיב ביה אמת - והא דכתיב (תהילים י״ט:י׳) משפטי ה' אמת, במשפטים הכתובים בתורה וציום לישראל קא משתעי, דלעיל מיניה כתיב פקודי ה' ישרים:
מוספי כל השנה הן שבח וסיפורי מעשה, אבל מוסף ראש השנה, מתוך שהוא מתפלל מלכיות, זכרונות, שופרות, מיפקד דינא טפי, ואל יפרוש אדם עצמו מן הצבור:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:13:3.english:
[With regard to] judgment, it is not written: "Truth" - And that which is written (Psalms 19:10): "The judgments of the Lord are truth" — it is speaking of the laws written in the Torah and commanded to Israel, for above it, it is written: "The precepts of the Lord are upright."
The Musaf [additional] prayers of the entire year are praise and the recounting of events, but [in] the Musaf prayer of Rosh Hashanah, since one prays [the blessings of] Malkhuyot [Kingship], Zikhronot [Remembrances], and Shofrot [Shofarot], judgment is scrutinized all the more, and [therefore] a person should not separate himself from the community.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:14:1.english: And not tomorrow to do them - For there are no mitzvot in the future [to come].

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:17:1.hebrew: לא עשו ישראל את העגל - כלומר, גבורים ושליטים ביצרם היו, ולא היה ראוי להתגבר יצרם עליהן, אלא גזירת מלך היתה לשלוט בם, כדי ליתן פתחון פה לבעלי תשובה. שאם יאמר החוטא: ״לא אשוב, שלא יקבלני״, אומרים לו: ״צא ולמד ממעשה העגל, שכפרו ונתקבלו בתשובה״:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:17:1.english: Israel did not make the [Golden] Calf - That is to say, they were mighty and masters over their [evil] inclination, and it was not fitting for their inclination to overpower them; rather, it was a decree of the King that it should rule over them, in order to give an opening of the mouth to penitents. For if the sinner should say, "I will not repent, because He will not accept me," they say to him: "Go and learn from the incident of the [Golden] Calf, for they denied [God] and [yet] were accepted in repentance."

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:17:2.english: Who would give that they had such a heart as this, etc. - It was said at Sinai. Consequently, they were mighty and stout of heart in their fear [of God].

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:18:2.hebrew: לבי חלל - יצר הרע חלל בקרבי, ואין לו כח לשלוט בקרבי:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:18:2.english: My heart is slain - The evil inclination is slain within me, and it has no power to rule within me.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:2:2.english: I cast it - I turned it out to graze.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:3:1.english: A companion [sokhenet] - An expression of warming.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:4:1.hebrew: מן השטים ועד הגלגל - עד באכם אל הגלגל, שהפלתי לפניכם שונאיכם:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:4:1.english: From Shittim to Gilgal - Until your arrival at Gilgal, where I cast down your enemies before you.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:6:1.english: For a moment in His anger - This shows that His anger is a moment.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:7:1.hebrew: סורייקי - נוקייש, לשון לע"ז, כמו חוטין חוטין. ולשון ישמעאל קורין לחוט סוריאק:
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:7:1.english: Streaks - Noquiés, an Old French word, [meaning] like threads. And in the language of Ishmael [Arabic], they call a thread suryak.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 4b:9:1.english: It is not proper conduct - To pinpoint the moment of His anger.

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4b:11:1.hebrew: כיון דאיכא צבורא דמצלי לא מדחי - פי' ר"ת: הא דמשמע הכא דמהני, אפי' כשהצבור מתפללין במקום אחר, היינו דוקא דלא מדחי; אבל אינה נשמעת אלא במקום שהצבור מתפללין, כדאמרינן בפ"ק דברכות (דף ו.): אין תפלתו של' אדם נשמעת אלא עם הצבור:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4b:11:1.english: Since there is a congregation that prays, it is not rejected - Rabbeinu Tam explains: That which is implied here, that it is effective even when the congregation is praying in another place, this is specifically that [his prayer] is not rejected; however, it is heard only in the place where the congregation is praying, as we say in the first chapter of Berakhot (6a): "A person's prayer is heard only with the congregation."

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4b:1:1.hebrew: ויודע דעת עליון - משמע מעצמו, ולא בנבואה; ולהכי פריך: דעת בהמתו לא הוה ידע:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4b:1:1.english: And knows the knowledge of the Most High - [This] implies [that he knew it] on his own, and not through prophecy; and for this reason [the Gemara] asks: [Is it possible that] he did not know the mind of his animal?

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4b:6:1.hebrew: רגע כמימרא - וא"ת, מה היה יכול לומר בשעה מועטת כזאת? ויש לומר, היה אומר כלם, והקב"ה הפכו ואמר מלך, כדכתיב (במדבר כ״ג:כ״א) ותרועת מלך בו. ורבי אליהו היה מפרש, שאין צריך רק להתחיל קללתו באותו רגע; תדע, שהיה רוצה להאריך בקללתו, כדאיתא בחלק (סנהדרין דף קה:): מברכותיו של אותו רשע אתה למד מה היה בלבו:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4b:6:1.english: A moment is [as long as] an utterance - And if you say: What could he [Balaam] have said in such a brief time? Then one can say: He would have said kallem [כלם, "destroy them"], and the Holy One, Blessed be He, inverted it [the letters] and said melekh [מלך, "King"], as it is written (Numbers 23:21): "and the shout of a King is in him." And Rabbi Eliyahu would explain that he needed only to begin his curse in that moment. Know [that this is so], for he wished to make his curse lengthy, as it is stated in [Perek] Chelek (Sanhedrin 105b): "From the blessings of that wicked one you learn what was in his heart."

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4b:6:2.hebrew: ה"ג ומנלן דרגע הוי ריתחיה שנאמר כי רגע באפו - ול"ג ומנלן דרגע כמימריה, דאם לא כן, היכי מפיק מהאי קרא דרגע כמימריה:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4b:6:2.english: This is the correct reading: "And from where do we know that a moment is [the duration of] His anger? As it is stated: 'For His anger is but a moment'" - And we do not read: "And from where do we know that a moment is [the duration of] an utterance?" For if that were not so, how could [the Gemara] derive from this verse that a moment is [the duration of] an utterance?

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4b:7:1.hebrew: בתלת שעי קמייתא - פי' בשלישית, כדאמרינן בסמוך: בשעה שהחמה זורחת, מלכי מזרח ומערב מניחים את כתריהן; ודרכן של מלכים לעמוד בג' שעות, כדאמרינן פ"ק דברכות (דף ט:):
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4b:7:1.english: In the first three hours - That is, in the third [hour], as we say nearby: "When the sun shines, the kings of the East and the West place their crowns [upon their heads]"; and it is the practice of kings to rise at three hours [into the day], as we say in the first chapter of Berakhot (9b).

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4b:9:1.hebrew: שמע מינה לאו אורח ארעא - לספרים דגרסי' ההוא עובד כוכבים, ניחא, דעובדי כוכבים לא מעלין ולא מורידין (לקמן עבודה זרה כו.); והוא שבקש לקללו, להזיקו בקללתו נתכוין ולא להרגו, ולא דמי להורדה לבור. ואפילו לספרים דגרסי ההוא מינא, אע"פ שהכופרים מורידין לבור, נמי ניחא, דודאי ביקש להרוג בקללתו; ומ"מ קאמר בתר הכי ש"מ לאו אורח ארעא, כי לא היה לו לדחוק בידי שמים ולהעניש מי שאינם רוצים להעניש, אע"פ שבזמן הבית הי' מותר להרגו בידים:
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 4b:9:1.english: Conclude from this that it is not proper conduct - According to the books that read "a certain idolater," it is understandable, for regarding idolaters, one neither raises nor lowers [them into a pit] (below, Avodah Zarah 26a); and [as for the fact] that he sought to curse him, he intended to harm him with his curse and not to kill him, and it is not comparable to lowering [someone] into a pit. And even according to the books that read "a certain heretic" — although regarding heretics one lowers [them] into a pit — it is also understandable, for he certainly sought to kill [him] with his curse. And nevertheless, he said afterward: "Conclude from this that it is not proper conduct," because he should not have pressed [the matter] through the hands of Heaven and punished someone whom they [in Heaven] do not wish to punish, even though in the time of the Temple it was permitted to kill him with [one's own] hands.
